newsitem.title: USA: Boeing might hire McDonnell Douglas - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Boeing might hire McDonnell Douglas - WSJ.

text.p: Boeing Co might hire McDonnell Douglas Corp to supply it with commercial-aircraft design, test and assembly services to help it deal with an overwhelming rise in orders from carriers, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday.
The two companies might sign an agreement by next week, according to "people tracking the developments," the newspaper said.
But there were still no signs from those people that Boeing might acquire Douglas Aircraft in the long term, it added.

Ronald Woodard, Boeing's commercial-airplane chief, told the newspaper the company was looking for "industry assist" contracts under which vendors would supply it with engineering work, parts and services.
"McDonnell Douglas is one of the companies we have talked to," he was quoted as saying. "There is no agreement in place. We are just at the front end of seeing if that's possible."
The newspaper said the two companies would study some large-scale contracts that Douglas could assume responsibility for the design and testing of most of the aircraft like a new 767-400.
Other things would include smaller design jobs, assembly and painting work and the lending of McDonnell employees to Boeing if the companies were to eventually sign an agreement, it added.
The newspaper said Boeing was thinking about subcontracting in order to avoid layoffs and factory closures once the boom in orders dies down.
A spokesman for McDonnell Douglas confirmed the talks with Boeing, it said.
